title: Economic progress is being reframed through work engagement, access to real jobs, and perceived life trajectory alongside GDP
source_unit: Gallup Economics 2026, Annual Report: leading indicators of economic growth
geography: Global Gallup World Poll adult population, with 2025 data and additional U.S. working-population samples

denominator.unit: Gallup companion indicators proposed alongside GDP: Gross Domestic Ambition, Gross Domestic Payroll to Population, and Gross Domestic Thriving

ambition.value: Gross Domestic Ambition measures the percentage of employees who are engaged and committed to their jobs in a culture of ambition

payroll.value: Gross Domestic Payroll to Population measures the share of the entire population aged 15 and older employed full time for an employer for at least 30 hours per week

thriving.value: Gross Domestic Thriving measures how people rate their lives today and how hopeful they feel about tomorrow

boundary.value: these are Gallup's proprietary companion measures and framework, not replacements for national accounts, causal estimates, or a complete welfare measure

observations.method: Gallup measurement framework combining GDP with World Poll and workplace indicators to capture economic ambition, full-time employer-based work, and present/future life evaluation.
observations.uncertainty: The framework's validity, comparability, and relationship to later growth or welfare outcomes require independent testing; definitions may differ from national statistical standards.
observations.subgroup: Adults aged 15 and older, employees, full-time workers, people outside the labor force, and populations with different work and life-evaluation conditions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Employment engagement and subjective thriving can improve without broad productivity growth, while GDP growth can coexist with low engagement or weak life evaluations.

observations.period: 2025 data reported in 2026; global work engagement and ambition

engagement.value: 20% of the world's workers are classified by Gallup as engaged—highly ambitious and committed to their jobs

culture.value: the Gross Domestic Ambition concept links workplace culture, employee engagement, innovation, growth, and competitiveness

work_quality.value: the indicator treats work engagement and ambition as distinct from simply having a job

analytic_signal.value: headline employment does not establish that workplaces provide motivation, agency, contribution, or a credible route to growth

observations.method: Gallup World Poll and workplace research used to construct the Gross Domestic Ambition indicator.
observations.uncertainty: Engagement is a modeled or surveyed construct influenced by question wording, culture, occupation, employment form, and local labor markets; it is not bargaining power or job quality by itself.
observations.subgroup: Employees, managers, occupations, sectors, countries, and workers with different levels of control, security, pay, and opportunity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low engagement may reflect temporary conditions, expectations, or cultural response styles rather than durable workplace dysfunction.

observations.period: 2025 data reported in 2026; full-time employer-based work and economic inclusion

payroll_to_population.value: 27% of the world's population aged 15 and older holds a full-time employer-based job of at least 30 hours per week

coverage.value: the measure counts the full population rather than only people already in the labor force, making access to stable employer-based work visible

inclusion.value: the indicator is intended to connect job growth to the breadth of economic participation rather than counting only unemployment or labor-force totals

analytic_signal.value: a country can show employment or output while a relatively small share of its adult population has the kind of full-time employer relationship the measure treats as a real job

observations.method: Gallup aggregate employment measure using the population aged 15 and older as denominator and a full-time employer-based work threshold.
observations.uncertainty: The threshold excludes self-employment, informal work, part-time work, unpaid care, education, and other valuable activities; it should not be interpreted as a universal definition of a real or good job.
observations.subgroup: Full-time employees, self-employed and informal workers, caregivers, students, older adults, people seeking work, and countries with different employment structures.
observations.counterinterpretation: Self-employment, flexible work, public transfers, household production, and part-time work can provide income or autonomy even when the indicator is low.

observations.period: 2025 data reported in 2026; present and future life trajectory

thriving.value: 35% of adults worldwide are classified by Gallup as thriving based on present and future life evaluations

trajectory.value: the measure combines how people believe their lives are going today with how hopeful they feel about tomorrow

economic_link.value: Gallup positions thriving alongside ambition, payroll-to-population, and GDP to connect economic conditions with perceived life direction

open_test.value: join GDP and prices, job access, work engagement, schedule and care time, housing and services, social connection, trust, life evaluation, and later mobility without treating subjective thriving as a causal outcome of one economic indicator

observations.method: Gallup World Poll life-evaluation data, with 2025 data collected between April and December 2025 and a civilian noninstitutionalized population aged 15 and older target.
observations.uncertainty: Subjective life evaluations vary with expectations, culture, current shocks, question framing, and response styles; they do not identify which institution or market condition caused the rating.
observations.subgroup: Adults across countries, age groups, income and employment situations, households, and people with different present and future expectations.
observations.counterinterpretation: High thriving can coexist with low material security in some contexts, while high GDP or employment can coexist with low hope or life satisfaction.

related_sources.claim: Gallup's World’s Most Important Problem report supplies a complementary aggregate public-attention route from economic security, work, governance, and safety to political judgment.
Gallup workplace research supplies broader context for engagement and workplace performance claims.
The official Gallup Economics page supplies the three proposed indicators, headline global values, source data, and methodology notes.

boundary: This record adds a measurement and lived-progress route from GDP and work access through engagement, full-time employer-based employment, life trajectory, and economic inclusion. It uses Gallup's aggregate survey and proprietary framework, not respondent-level records, national-account validation, bargaining-power measures, causal growth estimates, or proof that the three indicators predict future welfare equally across countries.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Gallup Economics 2026 page was reviewed for the three companion indicators, global headline values, conceptual framework, World Poll coverage, 2025 fieldwork window, and population definitions.
